**3B.9 Research Note: Abiy Ahmed in 2024**

Overall: **strongly negative**. The record shows domestic crises and spontaneous flare-ups were met mainly with emergency powers, mass detention, censorship, and covert coercive structures. I found only weak positive evidence in disaster-risk institution-building and limited oversight infrastructure, not in actual restraint during political crises.

- **Ethiopia authorities must stop using state of emergency law to silence peaceful dissent** | Amnesty International | 2024-02-19 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/ethiopia-authorities-must-stop-using-state-of-emergency-law-to-silence-peaceful-dissent/  
  - Amnesty said the state of emergency was being used to silence peaceful dissent through warrantless arrests, curfews, movement limits, and bans on assemblies and associations. This is direct evidence that a domestic crisis response was using coercion and fear rather than protection and restraint.  
  - QIDs: `3B.9`  
  - Also informs: `3B.5`, `3B.6`, `3B.8`

- **World Report 2024: Ethiopia** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-12 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia  
  - HRW described the Amhara emergency as granting broad warrantless-arrest, curfew, assembly-ban, and search powers, and said security forces repeatedly arrested critics and journalists. That is strong evidence against a restrained response to internal flare-ups.  
  - QIDs: `3B.9`  
  - Also informs: `3B.5`, `3B.6`, `3B.8`

- **Ethiopia’s Deepening Crackdown on Dissent** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-03-04 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/04/ethiopias-deepening-crackdown-dissent  
  - HRW reported arbitrary arrests, forced disappearance of EHRCO staff, and an atmosphere in which “no one” appeared safe from arbitrary detention. This shows the crisis response was producing fear and retaliation rather than suppressing violence in a rights-respecting way.  
  - QIDs: `3B.9`  
  - Also informs: `3B.5`, `3B.6`, `3B.8`, `3B.1`

- **Ethiopia: Halt Crackdown Against Human Rights Groups** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-06-18 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/06/18/ethiopia-halt-crackdown-against-human-rights-groups  
  - HRW said security and intelligence personnel followed, intimidated, and threatened human-rights workers at homes and offices. That is evidence of a chilling domestic security response, not a protective one.  
  - QIDs: `3B.9`  
  - Also informs: `3B.5`, `3B.6`, `3B.8`, `3B.1`

- **In Ethiopia, a secret committee orders killings and arrests to crush rebels** | Reuters via EHRC | 2024-02-27 | https://ehrc.org/in-ethiopia-a-secret-committee-orders-killings-and-arrests-to-crush-rebels-reuters/  
  - The EHRC head confirmed a secret security committee that interfered in the justice system and was linked to widespread human-rights violations. This is strong evidence of coercive, extra-legal domestic crisis management rather than restraint.  
  - QIDs: `3B.9`  
  - Also informs: `3B.5`, `3B.6`, `3B.8`, `3B.1`

- **Ethiopia: End the month-long arbitrary detention of thousands in Amhara Region** | Amnesty International | 2024-11-06 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/ethiopia-end-the-month-long-arbitrary-detention-of-thousands-in-amhara-region/  
  - Amnesty reported federal and regional forces rounding up thousands of civilians into makeshift detention camps. This is direct evidence of collective punishment and mass intimidation in response to unrest.  
  - QIDs: `3B.9`  
  - Also informs: `3B.5`, `3B.6`, `3B.8`, `3B.1`

- **Details of State of Emergency Declared by Gov't of Ethiopia** | ENA English | 2024-11-03 | https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/en_30124  
  - The proclamation centralized coercive authority, restricted CSOs and media suspected of helping “terrorist” groups, imposed ID and movement controls, and suspended normal judicial handling of enforcement. This is an official description of a broad coercive apparatus, not a narrow protection measure.  
  - QIDs: `3B.9`  
  - Also informs: `3B.5`, `3B.6`, `3B.8`

- **Ethiopia’s Disaster Risk Management Commission overhauls structure, policy, staffing, and technology** | ENA English | 2024-04-26 | https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4358046  
  - The government said it was improving emergency management and response capacity through institutional overhaul. This is weak positive evidence that some crisis capacity was being built, but it concerns disaster readiness more than political-crisis restraint.  
  - QIDs: `3B.9`  
  - Also informs: `3B.4`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`

- **Officials say new disaster-risk policy will help Ethiopia mitigate and respond to calamities using its own resources** | ENA English | 2024-07-05 | https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4724392  
  - Officials framed the policy as building preventive and response capacity inside state institutions. This supports a limited protection-oriented reading, but it does not outweigh the coercive handling of domestic unrest.  
  - QIDs: `3B.9`  
  - Also informs: `3B.4`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`

- **ICRC Bulletin: Ethiopia, January-June 2024** | International Committee of the Red Cross | 2024-09-13 | https://www.icrc.org/en/article/ethiopia-bulletin-january-june-2024  
  - The ICRC said it maintained dialogue and training on IHL/IHRL for the ENDF, police, militias, and other armed groups. This is a weak positive sign of harm reduction capacity, but it is training rather than proof of a restrained crisis response.  
  - QIDs: `3B.9`  
  - Also informs: `3B.4`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`

**Assessment**

- Negative evidence dominates: internal crises were repeatedly met with emergency rule, arbitrary detention, intimidation of critics, and secret coercive structures.
- Positive evidence exists, but it is mostly **institution-building** for disaster response, not proof that Abiy handled political violence with restraint.
- Search gap: I did **not** find reliable 2024 evidence that Abiy’s government consistently responded to domestic flare-ups with protection and restraint instead of collective punishment, censorship, or militarized control.
